conventions.convention: Canonical coordinates are ordered (q,p), ω = Σ dq_i ∧ dp_i, J has blocks (0,I;−I,0), and contraction of X_H with ω equals dH; consequently X_H = J∇H.
Local leapfrog is half-kick, full drift, half-kick, with composition read right to left; all intermediate configurations must lie in the open configuration set Q.
Symplectic Euler applies the kick before the drift, takes h > 0, and returns domain-failure when the resulting configuration leaves Q.

Implicit midpoint selects the unique stage root in the certified closed ball; its exact output is 2Z−z. Finite iteration outputs carry error certificates and are not asserted to be exactly symplectic.

The modified Hamiltonian is a fixed finite truncation on the star-shaped phase domain, with r = 1 for symplectic Euler and r = 2 for leapfrog or implicit midpoint; no infinite-series convergence is asserted.
For an empty compact set, uniform error is measured by its least nonnegative upper bound, equal to zero, rather than by a real supremum of the empty set.

load_bearing.statement: For fixed finite N ≥ r, the truncated pullback logarithm has Hamiltonian vector-field coefficients X_r,…,X_N with globally defined primitives H_r,…,H_N on the stated star-shaped phase domain; H_h^[N] = H + Σ h^j H_j is a finite modified Hamiltonian.

Under the stated C² closed-ball contraction hypotheses, the selected midpoint stage exists uniquely and its iterates satisfy the displayed stage and output error certificates. Under the additional C³, uniform branch and controlled-tube hypotheses, the exact selected map is symplectic, has one-step defect C|h|³, and finite-time error bounded by e^(L₁T)e₀ + CTe^(L₁T)|h|².

For V ∈ C³(Q), SPD M and the stated compact convex tube containing exact and numerical trajectories, stages and comparison segments, symplectic Euler and leapfrog have one-step defects bounded by C_E h² and C_V h³, and finite-time errors bounded by e^(LT)e₀ + C_E T e^(LT)h and e^(LT)e₀ + C_V T e^(LT)h², respectively.
For open Q, V ∈ C²(Q) and SPD M, the local kick and drift are C¹ on their open domains and their Jacobians A satisfy AᵀJA = J.

For fixed N ≥ r and the stated compact-domain, admitted-branch and comparison-tube hypotheses, the method and time-h finite modified flow differ uniformly on K by at most C_N|h|^(N+2), including the declared empty-K convention.

For fixed N ≥ r and the stated compact comparison tube containing the numerical and modified-flow endpoints and their joining segment, sufficiently small 0 < h ≤ 1 gives |H_h^[N](Φ_h(z)) − H_h^[N](z)| ≤ C₁h^(N+1), uniformly in z,h.

Midpoint stage existence, uniqueness, convergence and geometric tail bounds.
The complete Euclidean normed-space setting for the vector mean-value inequality.

Exact conservation of the finite modified Hamiltonian by its own local flow.
Existence of local integral curves of the smooth finite modified Hamiltonian field.

concerns.concern: The Statement says each step “has a C¹ Jacobian” under V ∈ C²(Q). This asserts more regularity than the hypotheses provide. Take d = 1, Q = R, M = 1 and V(q) = |q|^(5/2). Then V is C², but V''(q) = (15/4)|q|^(1/2) is not differentiable at zero. For any h > 0, the kick-then-drift map has Jacobian entry ∂p⁺/∂q = −hV''(q), which is not differentiable at zero, so its Jacobian is not C¹. The proof establishes a C¹ map with a continuous Jacobian satisfying the symplectic identity; it does not establish the Statement's C¹-Jacobian claim.

seams_checked.note: The prerequisite is contextual: no assigned item cites a Runge–Kutta-page proposition. The implicit midpoint algorithm explicitly defines its own implicit stage equation, and the assigned error proofs derive their Taylor coefficients directly. No explicit-midpoint result is substituted for implicit midpoint.

The constrained page and its listed items do not cite an assigned geometric-integration result as a logical supplier. Its prose keeps exact constraint solves, symplecticity, reversibility and conditional trajectory accuracy separate. In the reverse contextual direction, thm-finite-order-modified-energy-bound explicitly says its unconstrained result does not transfer to RATTLE.

Read the separable comparison-Hamiltonian definition and its leapfrog theorem. They use the local admitted kick/drift domain, cite the symplecticity proposition for its matrix identity, and retain C³ regularity, bounded derivatives and a compact convex tube for order two. They explicitly separate this canonical second-order comparison system from first-order Biot–Savart dynamics and make no modified-energy transfer. The supplier's overstrong Jacobian-regularity wording is recorded in concerns; this consumer only needs the valid C¹-map symplectic identity.
